Overview

TaskFlow is a B2B SaaS workspace where teams plan, track and ship work. It brings projects, tasks, deadlines and team activity into one dashboard, so leads can see what’s on track, what’s at risk and who’s overloaded — without a status meeting. I designed the UX, the UI and the design system.

MY ROLE

Mapped three user roles and the flows each one needs

Designed 24 screens across 9 views: dashboard, board, list, timeline, calendar, reports, team, task detail and settings

Built the design system: colour ramps, type scale and reusable components

Checked every colour pairing against WCAG 2.1 contrast

The problem

Work lives in five places — and leads only see problems in the weekly sync.

Tasks were spread across chats, sheets and personal to-do lists. Overdue work surfaced too late, and leads built reports by hand instead of unblocking people.

User flows

Personas

PERSONA

Ayesha

Product / Team Lead

Needs one answer every morning: “Are we going to hit the sprint?”

01

Leads need risk, not raw tasks

Portfolio-level KPIs, workload by teammate and reports they can share upward.

Makers need their next task

Clear priority and due dates, all context on one task page, and fewer pings.

03

Admins need fast setup

Invites, roles, billing and integrations in one consistent settings area.

Key decisions

01

KPI cards with trends on first load

Why: Leads get “are we on track?” before they scroll — overdue and at-risk work is visible, not buried.

02

One set of tasks, four views

Why: Board, list, calendar and timeline show the same data, so nobody keeps two versions in sync.

03

“New Task” in the topbar, on every screen

Why: Work gets captured the moment it comes up, instead of in a chat that gets lost.

Accessibility & privacy

Accessible by default

✓ Every colour pairing measured against WCAG 2.1

✓ Muted meta text (2.56:1) flagged — darkened to pass AA [Confirm]

✓ Status always has a label, never colour alone

Privacy & access (GDPR)

✓ Roles: admins, members and guests

✓ Guests see only the projects shared with them [Confirm]

✓ Activity log on every task: who changed what, and when

Outcome

Shipped · 2026 [Confirm]

TaskFlow shipped in 2026. It’s still early for hard numbers, so instead of guessing, I’m tracking the three signals below — they show whether the dashboard really replaces status meetings and manual reports.

What I’d track

01

Time leads spend building reports each week

02

Overdue tasks spotted before the weekly sync

03

Share of tasks created with “New Task”

What I learned

01

Structure before colour

Greyscale layouts settled the grid early, so 24 screens stayed consistent.

02

Measure contrast, don’t guess it

Checking every pairing showed the muted meta text failed AA — something I wouldn’t have seen by eye.

03

Test with real teams next

My next step is a test with 5 team leads: how fast can they find at-risk work?
